title: Chapter 53 — The First Meeting: Trade Discovery & The Account Pitch
intro: Trade discovery, the capability story, the terms conversation, and the first-project close.

sections.title: Trade Discovery
sections.content:
The first meeting with a trade prospect is discovery, not selling. You need to understand their business before you can serve it.

How many projects per year? What price range? Who selects the appliances — the builder, the designer, or the homeowner? What is their typical appliance budget per project? Who is their current supplier and what do they wish was different?

Listen more than you talk. The answers tell you exactly how to position your service.

sections.title: The Capability Story
sections.content:
After discovery, present what you offer — not a product catalog, but a service story. 'We provide spec consultation at three price tiers, same-day quoting, priority delivery coordination with your construction schedule, a single point of contact for everything, and warranty handling so your client never calls you about an appliance issue.'

Bring a physical spec package — three tiers with photos, specs, and pricing. Let them hold it. Let them see the quality of your presentation. First impressions in trade are lasting.

sections.title: Closing the First Project
sections.content:
The goal of the first meeting is not an annual contract. It is one project. 'Do you have a project coming up where I could show you how this works? Let me spec it for you — no commitment. If you like what you see, we will go from there.'

The first project is the audition. Deliver flawlessly on that one project and the relationship follows naturally.
